g.data-qualified-name: THE ASYMMETRY A DEBUGGER MUST NOT GET WRONG.asym
g.text: A REFUSAL IS NOT A HOLD
DUMP_CORE is gated on IF (run), not on
IF (dbg_hold_r). With the strap HIGH the
core is stopped in the debug sense and
Proved by mutation: re-gating DUMP_CORE on
the hold instead of the strap drops the
conformance to 6/22 - it is the step that

g.data-qualified-name: THE ASYMMETRY A DEBUGGER MUST NOT GET WRONG.asym2
g.text: bounded reads are NOT_READY while run=1
with NO FAULT - a sequencing rejection,
exactly like LOAD while running. So a
refusal latches nothing, and a host that
tries again after stopping the core gets
a clean answer with no cleanup needed.
READ_CPU IS THE ONE OP A DEBUGGER CAN
POLL ON A RUNNING CORE, and it is also the
one that reports insn. The subtlety, and
the reason this is drawn separately from
at next_pc while EXECUTING, at pc while
HELD, and at 0 at the boot stop. A
LANDING word, and at a freeze it reports
the LATCHED pipeline word. A harness that
collapses that fetch pipeline, so its insn
is the collapsed one - a TESTBENCH
section 3, notes for the vector author.
THE WIDTH CHANGE IS THE POINT OF R2, NOT A
at NATIVE widths and READ_CPU answers
while run=1, so the P3 liveness gap is
closed on the chip side: a host can
actually see a running program. The
manager ruled the ISA is the source of
truth, which is why A stayed 8 bits and
the host model's 13-bit A was a MODEL BUG.
FAULTS IS STICKY AND READ-BACK, so a host
sees a latched fault in the SAME header it
uses for registers. A sticky bit is not
cleared by a good read, and an
out-of-range READ latches exactly like a
write - so a host that probes past the end
once must call CLEAR_FAULT before its next
TWO OF THE THREE REAL DEFECTS R2 FOUND WERE
IN EXACTLY THIS AREA, which is why the
ceiling is drawn as a contract: an ODD DMEM
BYTE COUNT DROPPED ITS TRAILING BYTE (held
in a half-word register and never emitted,
leaving the response a word short of its
declared length), and the RESPONSE LAUNCH
NEVER FIRED because it sat inside an arm
that the launch itself cleared. A third
left an X on the MISO pad before the first
frame, which the pad-level TB caught. None
of the three was visible from a spec.
THIS IS THE SAME ASYMMETRY THE HOST-SIDE
MODEL CANNOT SHOW. A host model reaches a
held state by declaring debug_hold: true;
the CHIP reaches it by traffic, and the
traffic has to be legal. That is why the
held-core vectors had to DRIVE the debug
opcodes on the real pe_ctrl to build their
registers - the states 2 and 3 exist only
if the opcodes can produce them.
